title: The Orange Crush tribute, and one last pick-six
summary: Denver honored late Broncos great Tom Jackson before beating rival Las Vegas 38–24. With the Broncos ahead by seven late, Ja’Quan McMillian returned an interception for a touchdown.
preview: A tribute to a franchise legend, a division rival, and a one-handed interception return that turned a seven-point lead into a 14-point win.

timeline.label: Before kickoff
timeline.text: Denver paid tribute to late Ring of Famer Tom Jackson, including a moment of silence and recognition of his No. 57 legacy.

timeline.label: Late fourth quarter
timeline.text: With Denver leading by seven, Ja’Quan McMillian made a one-handed interception and returned it for a touchdown with 1:52 remaining.

unusual: The tribute came against a historic division rival, and a dramatic late defensive touchdown punctuated the victory—an echo of the existing Mike Ditka memorial-game case.
explanations: A moving tribute and a win can coexist without proving that the tribute caused the result. This is a documented coincidence, not evidence of orchestration.
questions: How often do teams win their first tribute game following a franchise legend's death?
Does any pattern remain after accounting for opponent strength and home-field advantage?
